issue.title: In-app assistant: tool approval required but no approval prompt is shown
issue.provider_name_version_configuration: not supplied in issue; not measured

released_reference.scope: Repository release source reference only; user installed artifact/build not byte-verified.

findings.fact: Chat invokes claude -p PROMPT, codex exec PROMPT, gemini -p PROMPT plus model/speed args. Shared process uses stdoutPIPE/stderrSTDOUT, inherited env/cwd and stdin=None in current provider calls. This is not a GUI-owned interactive approval channel or chat pseudo-terminal. Optional stdin_text helper writes once then closes; it is not a response bridge.
findings.qualification: stdin=None inherits launch context; do not say it is DEVNULL or universally unavailable. Actual provider CLI/version/config/policy decides tool behavior and remains unknown.

findings.fact: Worker exposes connecting/streaming/text/finished only; there is no approval-request ID/event or allow/deny reply API in this inspected chat route. ConsolePanel ignores stages; AIChatPanel labels only connecting/streaming. Streaming is emitted before iteration of lazy provider generator starts subprocess or receives data.
findings.impact: A blocked approval or no-newline prompt can remain presented as ordinary streaming/working instead of an actionable unavailable-permission state.

findings.fact: Exact leading Permission deny rule, Permission allow rule and Permission ask rule lines are discarded before display/failure-tail collection. Offline contract explicitly asserts this filtering.
findings.qualification: Issue body says approval required; that literal does not match these prefixes. No evidence identifies actual suppressed vendor line. Treat this as a diagnostic classification risk, not proven cause of reported failure; preserve harmless reminder filtering separately from real requests/denials.

findings.fact: Line reader blocks until newline/EOF; cleanup wait timeout occurs after output iteration ends, not an overall generation/approval deadline. Natural nonzero exit becomes ProviderFailed; exit0 text is an ordinary answer, with no structured approval-unavailable category.
findings.qualification: A model saying approval is required is not proof of an actual CLI approval event. Existing cancellation terminates tracked child; it cannot approve tools or prove their execution.

findings.fact: Default chat/error prompts contain no explicit disclosure that this GUI chat transport cannot present/respond to tool approval. SPEED_MAP/provider_args adds model selection only. Custom prompt is permitted and can differ.
findings.impact: No source-level capability notice prevents assistant from asking for a nonexistent GUI prompt repeatedly. This is an implementation gap aligned with the reported expectation, not a measured deterministic model response.

findings.fact: A separate POSIX pseudo-terminal SignInDialog and local stand-in tests exist for provider login. Chat stream implementations do not route through it.
findings.qualification: Login GUI existence does not establish tool-approval support; no login/auth/provider command was executed during this review.

future_acceptance_plan.proof_needed: GUI accurately identifies available capability or unavailable manual action, stops fake streaming indefinitely, does not declare a tool executed, and does not invent a shown dialog.

future_acceptance_plan.proof_needed: Current CLI auth instructions remain distinct; blocked gh issue create/pip install suggestions never automatically run. No unverified provider flags are added.
